targets.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier. Gog is the higher, closer-to-the-col summit of the Gog-Magog pair, and the route starts on its east face, reached by hiking across the snow below it and crossing the moat to the rock.
targets.descent_text: Rappel back down the east face to the base. Cross the moat and walk down the snowfield toward the Friendship Col trail and the hut.
targets.name: Gog East Face

targets.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, head up toward the lower Echo Glacier and pass below the small lakes on it to reach the notch on the northwest ridge of Quadrant. Dropping a little onto the east side of the ridge leads past the Rabbit Ears.
targets.name: NW Ridge Quadrant with Rabbit Ears Arete (s)
Outpost to Spire Traverse/ Quadrant Spire

targets.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, hike as if going to Friendship Col, then branch right toward the ridge. The line begins on the lowest reaches of the Shoestring Glacier, almost opposite Quadrant's south face, and gains the northern end of Sentinel's north ridge.
targets.name: Sentenel Peak - Shoofly Arete of North Ridge

targets.approach: From the Fairy Meadow base camp take the usual path through Friendship Col onto the glacier. Bear right past Sentinel's south ridge, to the col between East Peak and Pioneer, then climb the steep snow slope up the north-northeast ridge to the first prominent rock step.
targets.name: East Peak of Gothics - "North East" Ridge

targets.approach: Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier. From the Austerity Glacier reach the col between Adamant and Blackfriars, then head directly up the South Buttress.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route, since fixed tat marks every belay, or hike down from the summit on its west side and circle back to the Austerity Glacier.
targets.name: South Buttress, Adamant Mountain
targets.peak: South & West Faces (from Adamant or AusterityGlacier)

targets.approach: From the Mud Creek parking lot, walk the trail between two large square boulders, then up the well-built trail that leaves the gravel stream bed, taking the left fork. The trail passes the base of Small Walls and reaches the signed base of Ahren's Rock. The route is a slender crack just right of a large flake, partway down the rock from the Morning Glory area.
targets.name: Crack of Dawn

targets.approach: From the Goat Lake Main logging road, stay right at the Dianne branch junction and left at the D-branch junction (a four-wheel-drive road), then cross the bridge over the river. The flagged trail leaves on the right soon after the bridge, climbs through old-growth forest along the southwest ridge, crosses a large gully, and reaches Camp Radagast and then the foot of the wall. Then walk along the foot of the cliff to the start; the line is clear once you are below it.
targets.descent_text: Descend by rappelling On the Virg; carry two ropes and extra slings.
targets.name: On the Virg

targets.approach: From the Goat Lake Main logging road, take the D-branch road to the flagged trail that climbs through old-growth forest to Camp Radagast and the foot of Amon Rudh. The line sits at the far western end of the cliff; expect to thrash uphill before crossing the gully by the camp.
targets.name: The Slabs of Nim

targets.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, scramble east and down to find the large boulder, which is only moments away. A wide crack splits its south wall and angles upward from right to left; that crack is the route.
targets.name: Applebee Crack

targets.approach: Park at the BC Hydro campground at Seton Lake, cross the aqueduct and walk to the base of the wall. The route is on the left-hand side of the face.
targets.name: The Further Adventures of Trogdor the Burninator

targets.approach: From the overgrown clearcut low on the Rexford trail, head up and left to a forested ramp and follow it, on fourth class ground, to the base of the Chinese Puzzle Wall low on the west ridge of South Illusion Peak. The route takes the central line up the wall, beginning in the central crack system.
targets.name: Crouching Tiger

targets.approach: From the overgrown clearcut low on the Rexford trail, head up and left to a forested ramp and follow it, on fourth class ground, to the base of the Chinese Puzzle Wall low on the west ridge of South Illusion Peak. The climbing begins by traversing left across a loose, vegetated ledge to a ledge with a big tree.
targets.descent_text: Descend by way of Hidden Dragon.
targets.name: Manchu Wok

targets.approach: Follow the Sky Pilot approach to the Stadium Glacier and traverse west toward Copilot. Seppuku is on the north side of the peak, to the right of the main chimney that splits the face on the viewer's left; the first pitch climbs a right-arcing crack and slot that begins with a small roof.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the NE route from bolted anchors.
targets.name: Seppuku

targets.approach: Follow the normal Sky Pilot approach up to the Stadium Glacier, then cross easy snow slopes west to the foot of Copilot. Leave the snow and scramble up to the start of a corner, which is where the climbing begins; the scree can be extensive late in summer.
targets.name: West Ridge

targets.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground toward the base of the large formation under the Donkey Ears, following vague paths through the boulders. The route is on the South Tower, up the steep white wall beside and right of Thatcher Cracker, starting at the lowest point of the south face, on a short white wall under a large roof.
targets.name: Edwards-Neufeld

targets.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground to the base of the formation. Eeyore starts where Ears Between does and then bears right: take the fourth class ramp or the harder direct start to a ledge, with the Ears up and to the left and Eeyore up and to the right.
targets.name: Eeyore

targets.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground toward the base of the formation. The route starts in the main weakness between Lion's Way and Tiger's Trail, on fourth class ground, and later joins Lion's Way below its easy fifth class section.
targets.name: Lions and Tigers (Bad Kitty)

targets.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground toward the base of the Crescent Towers. The direct start is on the south face, below and a little left of a black boulder that sits at the top of the first pitch, which puts it nearly under the left Donkey Ear.
targets.descent_text: Bolted anchors at the top of the south summit allow a rappel to the north side.
targets.name: Thatcher Cracker

targets.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground and stay high past the base of the Donkey Ears. The route follows the vague buttress to the right of Lion's Way and to the left of the first Donkey Ear's steep wall, with an extra opening pitch starting from a grassy ledge.
targets.name: Tiger’s Trail

targets.approach: From the parking area at the northwest corner of Crest Lake, cross the highway and follow the trail east to the Crow's Nest. Look for the prominent arete; the route starts in a corner a couple of metres to its left.
targets.name: Levis

targets.approach: From the Crest Lake parking area, cross the highway and follow the trail east to the Crow's Nest, then go around the corner to the right and up the hill into the alcove. Climb the crack along the right edge of the staging platform.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.
targets.name: Faith Healer

targets.approach: The trailhead is at the head of Powell Lake and needs a boat transfer. From there bike up the Daniels valley beside the Daniels River, then bushwhack up to the subalpine on the east ridge. Cross a few bumps to a final bump on the ridge, which is descended on its left side by slippery fourth class, and the east face is then in view; campsites lie on the way to the base of the steep rock.
targets.descent_text: Downclimb or rappel the route ledge to ledge in short rappels.
targets.name: Mt Denman East face

targets.approach: From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the foot of the south face. The route is on the southwest side of the peak, and the first two pitches can be skipped by using the SW spur from the Dione couloir.
targets.name: Dehydrated on Dalwhinnie

targets.approach: From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the base of the peak. The route is on the west side of Dione.
targets.name: Drilling Dionysus

targets.approach: From the hut, go to Red Tit Col, then follow the broad Dione Glacier across the west flank under the peak's extended south ridge. The hut gives a clear view of the line. Crossing the moat to reach the rock can be hard in mid to late season. The route begins with the lower pitches of Dehydrated on Dalwhinnie, or climbs from the couloir approach to a two-bolt belay at the top of a blocky gully.
targets.descent_text: Scramble along the ridge to the summit ledge of Dione, then downclimb or rappel the southeast face.
targets.name: SW Buttress of Dione

targets.approach: From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the foot of the south face. The route begins from the Dione couloir, where an easy fourth class ramp leads onto the rock on the southwest side of the peak.
targets.name: SW Spur

targets.approach: From Lake of the Woods in the core of Cathedral Provincial Park, take the Goat Lake trail to the lake. Follow the right shore to its end, then angle left across a gravel fan toward Denture Ridge and climb the steep, crumbly scree and talus slopes southeast of the lake to a buttress on the left, just short of Denture Ridge's crest. The first pitch lies along the buttress's right flank, above a small cone of talus and grass, where a conspicuous crack and dike slants from right to left.
targets.name: Loose Caboose

targets.approach: From Lake of the Woods in the core of Cathedral Provincial Park, take the Goat Lake trail to the lake. Follow the right shore to its end, then angle left across a gravel fan toward Denture Ridge and climb the steep, crumbly scree and talus slopes southeast of the lake to a buttress on the left, just short of Denture Ridge's crest. The first pitch lies along the buttress's right flank, above a small cone of talus and grass, where a conspicuous crack and dike slants from right to left.
targets.name: Needs More Cowbell

targets.approach: From Lake of the Woods in the core of Cathedral Provincial Park, take the Goat Lake trail to the south end of the lake, then angle left across a gravel fan toward the scree and talus below Denture Ridge and climb to the crest. From the pass, drop down a short way on the far side and traverse left on ledges below the rock wall, continuing down and left to the south side, where the sunny south wall holds the route. Its first pitch leaves an open ledge up a crack.
targets.descent_text: The top is a broad grassy flat. Short rappels lead directly back to the pass on Denture Ridge; look for the anchors made of pins, nuts and cord.
targets.name: Patio Seating

targets.approach: From the Wall Creek meadow camp, hike directly up the loose slope by goat trails toward the Macabre-Grimface notch until the obvious cleft in the southeast flank of Grimface appears. Climb slabs to the foot of the chimney.
targets.descent_text: The usual descent is down the west ridge.
targets.name: Grimface SE Chimney

targets.approach: From the Wall Creek meadow camp, hike directly up the loose slope by goat trails to the southwest face of Matriarch. The route follows a prominent left-facing corner, with the Lady Fanny of Omaha SW Buttress to its right; rambling pitches lead to the corner.
targets.descent_text: Continue along the Matriarch-Macabre-Grimface traverse and come down Grimface's west ridge to return to the meadow.
targets.name: Matriarch SW Face

targets.approach: From the Wall Creek meadow camp, hike up the slope by goat trails to the notch southeast of the Grimface summit. The route starts just below the notch, up a chimney with a chockstone near the exit.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the northwest; cairns mark the easiest way down.
targets.name: SE Notch

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail and hike to the end-of-trail sign, then continue a few minutes on a faint path to Hermit Bluff, the cracked outcrop on the left. Backpacker is in the middle of the crag, a hand crack leading to a blocky corner.
targets.name: Backpacker

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail and hike to the end-of-trail sign, then continue a few minutes on a faint path to Hermit Bluff, the cracked outcrop on the left. Boo Bear climbs the arete of the bluff, second from the left among the routes.
targets.name: Boo Bear

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail and hike to the end-of-trail sign, then continue a few minutes on a faint path to Hermit Bluff, the cracked outcrop on the left. Hermit Crack is the obvious hand crack on the right side of the crag.
targets.name: Hermit Crack

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail and hike to the end-of-trail sign, then continue a few minutes on a faint path to Hermit Bluff, the cracked outcrop on the left. The routes are on its left side; Marmot Corner is the blocky corner on the far left.
targets.name: Marmot Corner

targets.approach: Take the established Hermit trail up until the cliff shows through the thinning timber, then contour west through several bushy gullies to a level bench on the Grizzly avalanche path. Cross the bench low to the boulder field, ford the creek, and climb to the left side of the small waterfalls above. From the foot of the falls traverse up and left along cairns to the upper boulder field, then cross it to the cliff base. The route is the clean, continuous crack system running up the centre of the face, with a large anchored ledge a short way up that can be reached from the left when snow lingers at the base.
targets.name: Pooh Crack
